Consult Summary:
- Evaluation of a new left elbow swelling (~1 week) suspected to be bursitis; plan includes NSAID therapy, blood tests to evaluate inflammatory/infectious/rheumatologic causes, and a follow-up appointment (in person or via telemedicine) after testing.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Swelling of the left elbow noticed about one week ago while in the shower; non-painful, slightly warm, and a sensation of fluid inside the joint. Patient can move the elbow normally and reports no clear injury.
- Onset/duration/progression: Onset ~1 week ago; symptoms not described as improving or worsening beyond initial observation; no trauma reported.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: No specific factors reported.
- Associated symptoms: None described.
- Review of systems: No fever, weight loss, night sweats, or systemic symptoms reported.
- Past Medical History: Osteoarthritis diagnosed by a GP a few years ago; otherwise healthy.
- Allergies: Peanut allergy.
- Medications: No regular medications.
- Family History: No rheumatologic diseases reported.
- Social History: Exercise: runs regularly (2–3 times per week); occupation described as desk-based. No other social history details provided.

Past Medical History:
- Osteoarthritis (diagnosed by GP, a few years ago).
- Peanut allergy.

Medications:
- Ibuprofen planned as treatment (see Assessment & Plan). Dose/route/frequency documented in plan below.
- No regular medications otherwise.

Allergies:
- Peanut allergy.

Social History:
- Regular athletic activity: running 2–3 times per week.
- Desk-based job.
- No other social history details provided.

Family History:
- No rheumatologic diseases reported.

Physical Examination:
- Left elbow: noticeable swelling; skin over swelling slightly warm; able to move elbow with ROM preserved; skin around elbow described as dry; tenderness localized to swelling area but not severely tender on exam; no mention of redness or systemic signs.
- No vitals provided.

Investigations:
- Blood tests to screen for inflammatory markers, infectious etiologies, and rheumatologic antibodies, plus urate (gout) assessment.
- Blood test forms to be sent to patient’s home with procedural instructions.
- Expected turnaround: results in approximately 5–6 days.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Left elbow swelling with warmth, nondraining and non-painful posture; exam suggests bursitis as a working diagnosis; septic arthritis not suspected at present.
  - Plan:
    - Start NSAID therapy: Ibuprofen 400 mg orally, twice daily after meals; instructions to discontinue if heartburn occurs.
    - Arrange blood tests: inflammatory markers, infection screen, rheumatologic antibodies, urate level.
    - Follow-up: arrange follow-up appointment after blood tests to review results (in clinic or via video/phone as preferred).
    - Education on red flag symptoms: seek urgent care if elbow becomes very red, very painful, or shows spreading redness or rapid worsening.
- Issue 2: Past medical history of osteoarthritis.
  - Plan: No active intervention beyond current management; continue to monitor as part of overall musculoskeletal health.
- Issue 3: Allergies.
  - Plan: Peanut allergy documented; no changes to management required at this time.

General Plan:
- Provide blood test completion and follow-up appointment after results.
- Monitor symptoms and contact clinic if deterioration occurs.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements: Vitals (BP, HR, temperature), detailed range-of-motion measurements, or prior imaging results if any; imaging not performed per transcript.
- Internal conflicts: None identified.
- Transcript quality: Clear, coherent; minor ambiguities around intra-articular fluid sensation, but overall consistent with bursitis assessment.
